# Northvale has blocked your withdrawals. We’re angry too.

**By Inês — Tuesday, 10 November 2026**

On Friday morning, without warning, Northvale Payments blocked every outgoing transfer from Pinha.

If you have tried to take out your own savings and found that you can’t, there is no softer way to say it: Northvale is preventing you from accessing your money, and preventing us from moving it for you.

You have every right to be angry. We are angry too — with Northvale for doing this, and with ourselves for leaving Pinha dependent on one payments partner. You do not have to lower your voice, write politely or stop being angry for us to take you seriously.

One woman from Porto wrote to us in capital letters. She has spent three years saving for a car deposit, and the dealership has given her until Friday, 13 November. I read her message on the metro and nearly cried. Not because she was shouting at us, but because she had every reason to.

That is what a blocked balance means. It is rent due, a medical bill, a deposit someone has worked towards for years. It is not an abstract payments problem.

Here is everything we know, what we are doing, and what you can do now.

## What happened

Northvale Payments is an e-money institution based in Vilnius. It holds Pinha customer money in a safeguarded account.

On **Wednesday, 4 November**, Northvale emailed us a notice of “commercial termination”, giving us **30 days’ notice**. The only explanation offered was a “risk appetite review”. That is a label, not a real explanation, but the notice at least appeared to give us time to arrange an orderly move.

Then, at **09:00 on Friday, 6 November**, Northvale blocked all outgoing transfers without warning. This went against its own 30-day notice. Deposits and round-ups also stopped, so no new money is being added through Pinha while access is frozen.

On Friday, our Northvale account manager stopped answering our calls. Their phone now goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian.

Breaking your own notice, blocking people’s savings without warning and then refusing to answer the phone is not a serious way to manage risk. In my view, it is cowardice.

## Where your money is

Your money has not disappeared.

It is held in a **safeguarded account, separate from Northvale’s own money**. Northvale cannot use those customer funds as its own money. The balances are still there, and the safeguarding arrangements are the reason we can say plainly that the money is not lost.

But we will not pretend that “safeguarded” means everything is fine.

Right now, you cannot withdraw it. Nor can Pinha move it while Northvale is blocking outgoing transfers. We do not have a separate route around that block. The money is protected from being spent by Northvale, but it is not accessible to you, and that is the part that urgently needs to change.

We know that being told your money is safe is not much comfort when you cannot use it.

## What we are doing

On **Saturday, 7 November**, we filed complaints with **Banco de Portugal** and the **Bank of Lithuania**, the central bank in Northvale’s home country. Rui has been in calls with our lawyers and Banco de Portugal, and we are continuing to press Northvale through every route available to us.

Those are necessary steps, but we are not going to present meetings and complaint references as progress when your money is still blocked. Progress means released funds.

We have also already signed with a new partner: **Ostra Bank, based in Lisbon**. Our aim is to migrate the customer balances and restore access through Ostra.

Before that migration can happen, we need two things:

1. Northvale must send the balances file.
2. Banco de Portugal must give the necessary approval.

Our current estimate for the migration is **10 to 15 working days**. Please read that as an estimate, **not a promise and not a release date**. We are still dependent on Northvale providing the file and on regulatory approval. We cannot honestly turn that estimate into a countdown from today, and we are not going to publish a date just because a date would look reassuring.

If the estimate changes, we will tell you. If one of these dependencies is holding everything up, we will tell you that too.

Alongside the full migration, we are trying to persuade Northvale to make **individual releases for urgent cases**. We cannot guarantee that Northvale will agree, or that any release will happen before a particular deadline. But we are trying, especially where waiting could cause immediate and serious harm.

## What you can do now

### If your situation is urgent

If you are facing something such as being unable to pay rent, an urgent medical expense, or losing your job and needing your savings to get by, email:

**urgent@pinha.example**

Use the subject line:

**URGENTE**

Tell us what you need to pay and what deadline you are facing. If there is another immediate, serious deadline — like the car deposit described above — please include it.

This email does not automatically release funds, and we do not want to give anyone false hope. It puts your case in front of us so we can pursue an individual release with Northvale.

### If you have another question or are waiting for support

Use our usual support channel. Since Friday, we have received around **1,900 support emails**. We have **three people** answering them, and the current reply time is approximately **two days**.

We know that waiting two days for an answer about your own money is frustrating. That is the actual position we are in, and we would rather tell you the truth than give you a response time we cannot meet.

Meanwhile, you do not need to keep attempting deposits or round-ups: those are stopped. Repeated withdrawal attempts will not override Northvale’s block.

### Your Pinha fee

We have cancelled the **Pinha monthly fee for November and December for everyone**.

You should not be paying us a monthly fee while you cannot access your savings.

### Where to find updates

We will publish an update on this blog **every Monday and Thursday until this is solved**, starting with the next update this Thursday.

That includes days when there is no substantial progress. If Northvale is still blocking the funds, if we are still waiting for the balances file, or if nothing has moved, we will say so. Silence while you wait for your own money is not acceptable.

## Our responsibility in this

I designed the Pinha screen that says:

**“Your money is always yours. Take it out anytime.”**

I believed those words when I designed them. Looking at that screen now makes me feel sick.

The first sentence still matters. It is your money. But the second sentence is not something you can do today, and I am not interested in protecting Pinha by quietly editing the wording or hiding behind the phrase “payments partner”.

We chose a structure with one partner and no backup ready. That was naive. It meant one company could take a decision that left all of you locked out. Northvale is responsible for blocking the transfers, but we are responsible for the trust we placed in that arrangement.

That mistake is ours, and we are sorry.

We are around 14,200 active users strong as a community, most of us in Portugal and some in Spain, but this comes down to individual lives. One person’s rent. One person’s prescription. Three years of round-ups that were supposed to become a car.

We are not going to tell anyone to calm down. Your anger is not a public-relations problem for us to manage. It is a reasonable response to being denied access to your savings.

The job in front of us is not to make you feel less angry. It is to get your money moving, to pursue urgent releases where we can, to complete the migration to Ostra, and to keep telling you exactly where things stand.

You need your money back within your reach. Until that happens, we will not treat this as resolved.

**Inês**  
Product designer, Pinha
